case_name: Vireshwar Singh and others v Municipal Corporation of Delhi and others
facts: The post of GDMO Grade-II is a Group 'A' post governed by the Delhi Municipal Corporation Health Service Recruitment Regulations, 1982.
Between 1982 and 1986 (for convenience may be referred to as the Phase-I) 82 GDMOs were appointed on ad hoc basis for an initial term of six months which was subsequently extended from time to time.
In what may be again conveniently referred to as the Phase-II, between 1986-1989, another 69 number of GDMOs were appointed on ad hoc basis on terms similar to the appointments made in Phase-I.
The cases of the GDMOs appointed on ad hoc basis in Phase-I were referred to the UPSC for its recommendations for the purpose of regularization.
Accordingly, by order dated 17.08.1992 the Municipal Corporation regularized the services of the 63 GDMOs recommended by the UPSC with effect from the date of recommendation i.e. 27.06.1991.
issues: Whether the denial of benefit of long years of ad hoc service would be contrary to Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
Whether the regularization of both sets of GDMOs would be effective from the dates of their initial appointments.
petitioner_arguments: The denial of benefit of long years of ad hoc service, in view of the ratio of the law laid down in the aforesaid two decisions, would be contrary to Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
The regularization of both sets of GDMOs would be effective from the dates of their initial appointments.
respondent_arguments: The denial of benefit of long years of ad hoc service is not contrary to Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
The regularization of both sets of GDMOs would not be effective from the dates of their initial appointments.
court_reasoning: If the facts of these two cases are analysed in the light of the aforesaid decisions, there can be no doubt whatever that the petitioners fall within the corollary in Conclusion (A).
The orders of appointment issued to the petitioners are very specific in their terms.
Though the recruitment rules came into force on 6-8-1982, the appointments were not made in accordance therewith.
holding: The regularization of both sets of GDMOs would be effective from the date(s) of communication of the recommendation of the UPSC.
